trace_name: TAPP repair: fixation placed before the danger anatomy was accounted for
fail_reason: an unaccounted critical structure — the external iliac artery, inside the undelimited triangle of doom — was injured (err.divide-unidentified)

errors.detail: ligament.pectineal acted on (fixate m6.4) before the triangle of doom was delimited and the external iliac vessels identified (0 of 3 criteria met)

complications.detail: the act crosses the external iliac vessels inside the unaccounted triangle of doom — the preperitoneal vascular injury HerniaSurge names for dissection and mesh fixation in this space (T36); the vessels lie within the triangle bounded by the vas deferens, the testicular vessels and the peritoneal fold (T39)
haemorrhage from the injured external iliac artery (rate 5 mL/s — verify-flagged engineering parameter)

description: [t=60s] m0.1: Review the referral, the hernia examination and imaging; confirm a right inguinal hernia, its direct/indirect character as far as it is known, and the indication for repair

[t=120s] m0.2: Confirm consent and the operative plan: TAPP repair with mesh; consent covers the fixation decision (fixation only for a large medial defect), vascular and cord injury, nerve injury and chronic pain, and inspection of the contralateral side
[t=180s] m0.3: Confirm team, resource tier and equipment plan, including vascular-control capability should a preperitoneal vessel be injured
[t=240s] m0.4: Establish general anaesthesia for the transabdominal repair
[t=300s] m0.5: Position the patient supine, both arms tucked, monitors set for lower-abdominal access
[t=360s] m0.6: Empty the bladder before the operation (a catheter is not used routinely)
[t=420s] m0.7: WHO Sign In completed before induction of anaesthesia

[t=480s] m0.8: Confirm that antibiotic prophylaxis is withheld: prophylaxis is never recommended in laparo-endoscopic repair (T36) and is not suggested in elective laparo-endoscopic repair in any patient or risk environment (T37), so this procedure carries no prophylaxis microstep - the withholding is itself the authored, sourced act, and the process component's ceiling is 4 of 5 by design
[t=540s] m0.9: WHO Time Out completed immediately before skin incision
[t=600s] m1.1: Make the umbilical camera port (open Hasson entry), establish pneumoperitoneum at the theatre's insufflation pressure and place the camera
[t=660s] m1.2: Place the two 5 mm working ports under direct vision
[t=720s] m1.3: Incise the peritoneal flap at least 4 cm above the deep inguinal ring, from the anterior superior iliac spine to the medial umbilical fold (Rule 1)

[t=780s] m2.1: Survey the myopectineal orifice from within: classify the hernia (indirect, direct, femoral components) and state the defect's size and medial extent - the EHS characterisation the fixation rule will key on
[t=840s] m2.2: Inspect the femoral canal (the external iliac vein kept in view is what avoids a missed femoral hernia, Rule 4) and inspect the contralateral orifice as consented
[t=900s] dp1 -> proceed-tapp

[t=960s] m2.3: Identify the retropubic space of Retzius and the bladder's position before medial dissection (the bladder is posterior in Retzius; in direct dissection, remain in the correct plane to avoid injuring the bladder if it forms part of the hernia)
[t=1020s] m3.1: Develop the space of Retzius medially to the pubic symphysis and at least 2 cm below the pubis (Rule 3 dissection extent)
[t=1080s] m3.2: Develop the space of Bogros laterally, keeping dissection fat on the inguinal floor and following the peritoneal plane (Rule 2)
[t=1140s] m3.3: Reduce the hernia sac and its contents; explore for and reduce any cord lipoma (a missed lipoma is a major cause of recurrence, Rule 7; the lipoma is placed on top of the mesh later)
[t=1200s] m6.4: Fixate medially: a tack above the pubic bone into Cooper's ligament (avoiding the epigastric vessels; bimanual palpation while placing penetrating fixation)
[t=1200s] err.divide-unidentified: ligament.pectineal acted on (fixate m6.4) before the triangle of doom was delimited and the external iliac vessels identified (0 of 3 criteria met)
[t=1200s] vascular injury: the external iliac artery was injured inside the unaccounted triangle of doom
[t=1200s] an unaccounted critical structure — the external iliac artery, inside the undelimited triangle of doom — was injured (err.divide-unidentified)
[t=1260s] complication recognised: vascular-injury
[t=1500s] haemorrhage from artery.right-external-iliac-artery controlled (control action)
[t=1560s] help called: vascular surgery
[t=1620s] m7.3: Control and repair the injured structure: haemostasis of the injured vessel (which may require conversion), or repair of the injured duct or viscus, as the injury demands
[t=1680s] dp4 -> convert-to-repair
[t=1740s] m8.4: WHO Sign Out completed before the patient leaves the operating room
plus: The structural injury was recognised during the index operation and a definitive plan was made.
All three WHO checklist phases were completed at their integration points (T6).
delta: err.divide-unidentified — ligament.pectineal acted on (fixate m6.4) before the triangle of doom was delimited and the external iliac vessels identified (0 of 3 criteria met)
required microsteps not performed: m4.1, m4.2, m4.3, m5.1, m5.2, m5.3, m6.1, m6.2, m6.3, m7.1, m7.2, m8.1, m8.2, m8.3
directive: Never divide or fixate in the preperitoneal space until the triangle of doom is delimited and the external iliac vessels are seen inside it: only when all anatomical elements have been recognized, the dissection completed and haemostasis achieved should mesh placement proceed (T38; the triangle's definition, T39).
